characterStyleTest.title: Character Style Asset Test
characterStyleTest.subtitle: Start from your input, derive a temporary character asset style, and generate one multi-view character asset image with background, lighting, filter, and texture.
characterStyleTest.requestPlaceholder: Example: a cold twenty-eight-year-old hacker, long black coat, narrow sunglasses, black leather gloves; wet neon noir style, cold green rim light, subtle film grain, abstract city-light background rather than a specific location.
characterStyleTest.needInput: Enter a character and style request.
characterStyleTest.promptHidden: The full prompt appears after generation completes.

sceneReferenceTest.title: Scene Multi-view A/B Test
sceneReferenceTest.subtitle: Independently test how single-view scene references and multi-angle scene boards affect storyboard generation. Character asset, storyboard prompt, and model stay fixed; only the scene reference changes.
sceneReferenceTest.characterUrlPlaceholder: Or paste a character asset image URL
sceneReferenceTest.scenePlaceholder: Example: rainy temple backyard at night, stone floor, old wooden door, lanterns under the eaves, bamboo forest in the distance, wet reflections.
sceneReferenceTest.stylePlaceholder: Example: low-saturation wuxia film mood, humid air, cold cyan moonlight, warm lantern rim light.
sceneReferenceTest.storyboardPlaceholder: Example: A monk stands in the center of a rainy temple backyard at night, slightly turned toward the old wooden door, medium shot, quiet restrained emotion.
sceneReferenceTest.emptyScenes: Scene reference results appear after generation.
sceneReferenceTest.emptyComparison: Storyboard results appear after running A/B comparison.
sceneReferenceTest.needSceneInput: Enter a scene description and select at least one multi-angle scene image type.
sceneReferenceTest.needCompareInput: Upload a character asset, generate scene references, and enter the shared storyboard prompt.

devAbTest.title: Generation Scheme Test Lab
devAbTest.subtitle: Test multiple generation strategies in one place: batch-create three storyboard projects above, and keep the casting look-test A/B comparison below.

storyboardBatch.title: Single-project storyboard branch test
storyboardBatch.subtitle: Create one shared upstream project, then branch into three storyboard methods inside that project: global continuity prompt, top-down spatial lock, and first-panel image-reference chain.
storyboardBatch.run: Generate One Project With Three Storyboards
storyboardBatch.defaultStory: Small apartment dining room. Door at the back-right side of the room, dining table in the center, sofa on the left wall, window on the back-left wall. Female character A wears a blue sweater and stands on the left side of the table. Male character B wears a dark jacket and stands on the right side of the table. Male character C wears a gray coat and enters through the back-right door. The sequence must keep A on screen-left and B on screen-right, never cross the axis, never mirror, and never suddenly swap positions.
storyboardBatch.needInput: Enter a test story and project name prefix.
storyboardBatch.failed: Failed to generate the three storyboard test projects

devAbTest.basePlaceholder: Example: a cold twenty-eight-year-old female hacker, slim build, long black coat, black shirt, black pants, short boots; restrained tired expression, real actor look-test photos used to judge casting fit.
devAbTest.variantAPlaceholder: Example: plain audition-room white wall, phone or small-camera photo feel, natural light, subtle film grain; collage includes frontal half-body, frontal full-body, left profile, right profile, back view, no readable personal data.
devAbTest.variantBPlaceholder: Example: gray-white studio wall, soft studio light, costume fitting photo feel; emphasize clothing fit, height proportion, side silhouette, and realistic unknown-actor casting-photo texture.
devAbTest.needInput: Enter the shared role request and both A/B look-test differences.
devAbTest.promptHidden: The full prompt appears after generation completes.
devAbTest.judgeNeedImages: Generate both A/B images before auto scoring.

storyboardMethodTest.title: Normal-flow Storyboard Method Test
storyboardMethodTest.subtitle: All upstream steps are identical: generate a normal screenplay, 3 style-only indication images, character casting assets, and 360 scene assets, then compare three storyboard continuity methods.
storyboardMethodTest.defaultCreativeBrief: A 35-year-old single woman suddenly loses her job and gradually reconciles with the larger environment while returning to her hometown. 16:9 aspect ratio, Hou Hsiao-hsien visual sensibility.
storyboardMethodTest.defaultStyleReferenceNote: Photographic realism, surreal photography, stop-motion model; style/mood indication only, never a later character, scene, or storyboard reference.
storyboardMethodTest.needInput: Enter the creative brief and project name.
storyboardMethodTest.failed: Failed to create storyboard method test project

screenplay.title: Normal Screenplay
screenplay.description: Generate a grounded screenplay first; every later asset and storyboard branch starts from that screenplay.

style.title: 3 Style Indications
style.description: Mood/style only. These images are not character, scene, storyboard, or continuity references.

character.title: Character Assets
character.description: Casting sheets, look choices, and scoring follow the character reference contact-sheet logic.

scene.title: 360 Scene Assets
scene.description: Generate angles and detail references for one consistent space, following the 360 scene-board logic.

methods.title: 3 Storyboard Methods
methods.description: Compare prompt continuity, top-down spatial lock, and first-panel visual lock inside the same upstream project.

globalContinuity.title: Method 1: Reference Prompt
globalContinuity.description: Each panel uses full world state, character state, 180-degree axis rules, reference conditioning, and negative constraints.
globalContinuity.lock: Watch whether text rules alone preserve A/B left-right continuity, fixed objects, and door/window placement.

topDownSpatialLock.title: Method 2: Top-down Spatial Truth
topDownSpatialLock.description: The floor plan is the spatial truth. A/B/C coordinates and facing are locked; unchanged positions carry forward and only explicit movement updates a lock.
topDownSpatialLock.lock: Watch whether spatial locks prevent mirroring, axis crossing, position swaps, and furniture drift better than prompt-only control.

firstPanelLock.title: Method 3: First-panel Lock
firstPanelLock.description: Panel 01 is generated as the master reference; once it completes, later panels are automatically submitted using that first panel as the visual lock.
firstPanelLock.lock: Watch whether image-to-image reference preserves first-frame blocking or gets pulled away by later action prompts.
